This is a sample text document for testing the InsightFlow AI upload pipeline.

It contains multiple paragraphs to ensure the chunking logic works correctly.
The document should be parsed by TextLoader and split into chunks by RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter.

Here is some more content to make sure we have enough text to create at least a couple of chunks.
RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) is a technique that combines information retrieval with 
text generation. It allows AI models to answer questions based on specific documents rather than 
relying solely on their training data. This makes answers more accurate and grounded in facts.

The process works like this: first, a document is split into smaller chunks. Each chunk is then 
converted into a numerical representation called an embedding. These embeddings are stored in a 
vector database. When a user asks a question, the question is also converted to an embedding, 
and the most similar document chunks are retrieved. Finally, these chunks are passed to an LLM 
along with the question, and the LLM generates an answer based on the retrieved context.
